title: Arrow-target Cartesian fibration and pullback squares
statement: Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, mapping spaces and limiting cones from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and Cartesian edges and fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $C$ be a quasicategory in a fixed universe and assume that every cospan in $C$ has a pullback, meaning a limiting cone on that cospan. Put $\operatorname{Arr}(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ and let $t=\operatorname{ev}_1:\operatorname{Arr}(C)\to C$ be target evaluation. Then $t$ is a Cartesian fibration. An edge of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$, viewed as a coherent square $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1\to C$, is $t$-Cartesian if and only if this square is a pullback. For $f:c'\to c$ and an object $z\to c$ of the target fiber, the Cartesian lift over $f$ with target $z\to c$ is equivalent in the fiber at $c'$ to the pullback projection $z\times_c c'\to c'$. All pullbacks here are infinity-categorical pullbacks; no terminal object, presentability, or choice of pullback objects is assumed.

source.place: HTT Lemma 6.1.1.1, printed pp. 531-532 (PDF pp. 549-550); transport discussion immediately following it. Also GHN Remark 9.5. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this quasicategory theorem.

proof.text: First, $\operatorname{Arr}(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ is a quasicategory by the functor-category result. The endpoint inclusion $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is degreewise injective, so exponentiation gives an isofibration $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(\{1\},C)= C$; hence $t$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories. Its fiber over $c$ is the degreewise pullback $\operatorname{Arr}(C)\times_C\{c\}$: its objects are the arrows $z\to c$, and its simplices are the coherent diagrams $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to C$ whose restriction to $\Delta^n\times\{1\}$ is constant at $c$. It is a quasicategory, since the inner horn lifting of $t$ restricts to it.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.1.1, first paragraph; Definition 2.4.1.1 and Proposition 2.4.1.8; read online 2026-10-17

proof.text: Let $f:c'\to c$ and let $v':z\to c$ be an object of the target fiber. By hypothesis choose a limiting cone on the cospan $z\to c\leftarrow c'$, presented by a coherent square with apex $P=z\times_cc'$ as in [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion]; read along the cospan direction it is an edge $e_0:v\to v'$ of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$ with $v:P\to c'$ the pullback projection and $t(e_0)=f$. To show that $e_0$ is $t$-Cartesian, by [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-criterion] it suffices that for every object $u:w\to d$ of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$ the square with top $\operatorname{Map}(u,v)\to\operatorname{Map}(u,v')$ (postcomposition with $e_0$), bottom $\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c)$ (postcomposition with $f$) and vertical maps induced by $t$ is a homotopy pullback. By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square], naturally in the second arrow and compatibly with the endpoint projections, $\operatorname{Map}(u,v)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(w,P)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c')}\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c')$ and $\operatorname{Map}(u,v')\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)}\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c)$, with $t$ the projection to the second factor. Hence the square $\operatorname{Map}(u,v')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ (precomposition with $u$) is a homotopy pullback, and so is the square $\operatorname{Map}(u,v)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,P)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c')$. Since the cone is limiting, [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion] with test object $w$ says that the square $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,P)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ is a homotopy pullback. Pasting these last two squares by [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] makes the rectangle $\operatorname{Map}(u,v)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(d,c')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ a homotopy pullback. This rectangle is also the composite of the criterion square with the homotopy-pullback square for $v'$, since postcomposition with $e_0$ followed by the source projection is the source projection followed by composition with $P\to z$. By the 'left iff outer' clause of [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], the criterion square is a homotopy pullback, so $e_0$ is $t$-Cartesian.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.1.1, pullback construction and proof; Proposition 2.4.4.3; read online 2026-10-17. Mapping-space pullback criterion: Cisinski CatLR Theorem 6.6.9 and Remark 6.6.11, as stated in lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion

proof.text: Conversely, let $e:(a\to b)\to(z\to c)$ be a $t$-Cartesian edge of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$, viewed as a coherent square with apex $a$ on the cospan $z\to c\leftarrow b$. Fix an object $w$ of $C$ and apply [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-criterion] to the object $1_w:w\to w$ of $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$: the square $\operatorname{Map}(1_w,a\to b)\to\operatorname{Map}(1_w,z\to c)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,b)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ is a homotopy pullback. By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square], $\operatorname{Map}(1_w,z\to c)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ (precomposition with $1_w$) is a homotopy pullback, and pasting by [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] makes the rectangle $\operatorname{Map}(1_w,a\to b)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,b)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)$ a homotopy pullback. Precomposition with the degenerate edge $1_w$ is homotopic to the identity by the unitality of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Hence in $\operatorname{Map}(1_w,a\to b)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(w,a)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_C(w,b)}\operatorname{Map}_C(w,b)$ the projection to $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,a)$ is an equivalence: a path pullback along a map homotopic to the identity retracts onto the other factor by contracting the path. By two-out-of-three, the comparison $\operatorname{Map}_C(w,a)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(w,z)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_C(w,c)}\operatorname{Map}_C(w,b)$ of the square is an equivalence. This holds for every $w$, so [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion] says that the square is a limiting cone, a pullback. With Step 2, a $t$-Cartesian edge is precisely a pullback square. Every edge $f:c'\to c$ and every $z\to c$ have the Cartesian lift $e_0$ of Step 2, so by Step 1 and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], $t$ is a Cartesian fibration.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.1.1, converse characterization; Proposition 2.4.4.3; read online 2026-10-17. Mapping-space pullback criterion: Cisinski CatLR Theorem 6.6.9 and Remark 6.6.11

proof.text: Let $e:y\to v'$ be any $t$-Cartesian edge over $f$ with target $v'=(z\to c)$, and let $e_0:v\to v'$ be the lift of Step 2, $v=(z\times_cc'\to c')$. Write $F$ for the fiber at $c'$, a quasicategory by Step 1. For $x$ in $F$ put $H(x)=\operatorname{hofib}_f(\operatorname{Map}(x,v')\to\operatorname{Map}_C(c',c))$. By [lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-fiber], postcomposition with $e_0$ gives an equivalence $\phi_0:\operatorname{Map}_F(x,v)\to H(x)$, and postcomposition with $e$ an equivalence $\phi:\operatorname{Map}_F(x,y)\to H(x)$. The edge $e$ with the constant path at $f$ is a point of $H(y)$, so there is $g\in\operatorname{Map}_F(y,v)$ with $\phi_0(g)$ in the component of $e$. Likewise there is $g'\in\operatorname{Map}_F(v,y)$ with $\phi(g')$ in the component of $e_0$. Precomposition with an edge of $F$ maps $H(x)$ to $H(x')$, since its image in $C$ is the degenerate edge at $c'$. By the associativity and unitality of the composition classes of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], applied in $\operatorname{Arr}(C)$ and in $C$ compatibly with $t$, $\phi_0(g\circ g')=e_0\circ(g\circ g')$ lies in the component of $(e_0\circ g)\circ g'$, hence of $e\circ g'=\phi(g')$, hence of $e_0=\phi_0(1_v)$, all in $H(v)$. Since $\phi_0$ is bijective on components, $[g\circ g']=[1_v]$ in $hF$. Symmetrically $[g'\circ g]=[1_y]$ using $\phi$. By the invertibility clause of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], $g'$ is an equivalence edge of $F$ from $v$ to $y$. Thus every Cartesian lift over $f$ with target $z\to c$ is equivalent in the fiber at $c'$ to the pullback projection $z\times_cc'\to c'$. This uses only the cospan hypothesis; no global choice of pullbacks is made and no transformation-level transport is asserted.

The HTT PDF was read online and is not archived locally; no statement hypotheses beyond cospan pullbacks were added. Maintainer reader fix (2026-10-17): Steps 2-3 now cite the existing same-unit lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion for the path-model mapping-space test of a cospan limit, instead of the duplicate new node lem-coef-infinity-space-cospan-limit-path-pullback (dropped) and lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits. Step 3 now concludes the Cartesian-fibration property explicitly. Step 4 now proves the uniqueness of Cartesian lifts in the fiber, which the statement asserts, via lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-fiber and lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition. Step 1 states the fiber exactly, without calling it a full subcategory.

The statement is true, with no hypothesis added. Small cases tested: posets with meets, Set, Δ0, the empty quasicategory, and identity base edges. Fixes: (1) C5/D. The new node lem-coef-infinity-space-cospan-limit-path-pullback duplicates the existing same-unit node lem-coef-kan-nerve-pullback-recognition (case q=id) together with the uniqueness of terminal cones, and it also cited def-cbc for 'the infinity category of spaces', which that node does not define (B3). I dropped it. Steps 2-3 now cite the existing lem-coef-infinity-terminal-pullback-criterion (path-model mapping-space test for cospan cones) in place of the dropped node and yoneda-presheaf-limits, with the pasting written out square by square. Step 3 now uses the 1_w collapse (unitality in lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition) and two-out-of-three, because pasting alone cannot give the needed square. (2) C1/E5. Step 4 did not prove that Cartesian lifts are unique up to equivalence in the fibre, which the statement asserts. It is now proved with the existing lem-coef-infinity-cartesian-mapping-fiber and lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition. Step 1's fibre description is made exact (the fibre is not full in Arr(C)). (3) In the Cartesian mapping-criterion node, source.place and blueprint.from.place no longer call HTT 2.4.4.3 a dual, and HTT 2.4.1.8 is cited as a Proposition. That node is kept: it is not a one-line specialization of the cocartesian sibling, because passing to the opposite category changes right-pinched mapping spaces into left-pinched ones.
